author: Thomas à Kempis
title: How a desolate man ought to commit himself into the hands of God

notes.text: (1) Psalm lxxxviii. 15. (2) Job xxix. 3. (3) Psalm xvii. 8. (4) Psalm cxix. 71. (5) Job xiii. 2.

verses.text: O Lord, Holy Father, be Thou blessed now and evermore; because as Thou wilt so it is done, and what Thou doest is good.
verses.modernizedText: O Lord, Holy Father, be blessed now and forever, because as You will, so it is done, and what You do is good.

verses.text: Let Thy servant rejoice in Thee, not in himself, nor in any other; because Thou alone art the true joy, Thou art my hope and my crown, Thou art my joy and my honour, O Lord.
verses.modernizedText: Let Your servant rejoice in You, not in himself or in any other; because You alone are the true joy, You are my hope and my crown, You are my joy and my honor, O Lord.

verses.text: What hath Thy servant, which he received not from Thee, even without merit of his own?
verses.modernizedText: What does Your servant have that he did not receive from You, without any merit of his own?

verses.text: Thine are all things which Thou hast given, and which Thou hast made.
verses.modernizedText: Yours are all things that You have given and made.

verses.text: I am poor and in misery even from my youth up,(1) and my soul is sorrowful unto tears, sometimes also it is disquieted within itself, because of the sufferings which are coming upon it.
verses.modernizedText: I am poor and in misery even from my youth,(1) and my soul is sorrowful to tears; sometimes it is also troubled within itself because of the sufferings coming upon it.

verses.text: I long after the joy of peace; for the peace of Thy children do I beseech, for in the light of Thy comfort they are fed by Thee.
verses.modernizedText: I long for the joy of peace; I ask for the peace of Your children, for in the light of Your comfort they are fed by You.

verses.text: If Thou give peace, if Thou pour into me holy joy, the soul of Thy servant shall be full of melody, and devout in Thy praise.
verses.modernizedText: If You give peace, if You pour holy joy into me, the soul of Your servant will be full of melody and devout in Your praise.

verses.text: But if Thou withdraw Thyself as too often Thou art wont, he will not be able to run in the way of Thy commandments, but rather he will smite his breast and will bow his knees; because it is not with him as yesterday and the day before, when Thy candle shined upon his head,(2) and he walked under the shadow of Thy wings,(3) from the temptations which beset him.
verses.modernizedText: But if You withdraw Yourself, as too often You do, he will not be able to run in the way of Your commandments; instead he will beat his breast and bow his knees, because it is not with him as yesterday and the day before, when Your candle shone upon his head,(2) and he walked under the shadow of Your wings,(3) away from the temptations that beset him.

verses.text: O Father, righteous and ever to be praised, the hour cometh when Thy servant is to be proved.
verses.modernizedText: O Father, righteous and forever to be praised, the hour comes when Your servant is to be tested.

verses.text: O beloved Father, it is well that in this hour Thy servant suffer somewhat for Thy sake.
verses.modernizedText: O beloved Father, it is good that in this hour Your servant should suffer something for Your sake.

verses.text: O Father, evermore to be adored, as the hour cometh which Thou foreknewest from everlasting, when for a little while Thy servant should outwardly bow down, but always live inwardly with Thee; when for a little while he should be little regarded, humbled, and fail in the eyes of men; should be wasted with sufferings and weaknesses, to rise again with Thee in the dawn of the new light, and be glorified in the heavenly places.
verses.modernizedText: O Father, forever to be adored, the hour comes which You knew from eternity, when for a little while Your servant should bow down outwardly but always live inwardly with You; when for a little while he should be little regarded, humbled, and fall in the eyes of men, and be worn down by sufferings and weaknesses, only to rise again with You at the dawn of the new light and be glorified in heavenly places.

verses.text: O Holy Father, thou hast ordained it so, and so hast willed it; and that is done which Thou Thyself hast commanded.
verses.modernizedText: O Holy Father, You have ordained and willed it so, and what You Yourself have commanded is done.

verses.text: For this is Thy favour to Thy friend, that he should suffer and be troubled in the world for Thy love’s sake, how often soever, and by whomsoever and whosoever Thou hast suffered it to be done.
verses.modernizedText: For this is Your favor to Your friend: that he should suffer and be troubled in the world for the sake of Your love, however often, by whomever and through whatever means You have permitted it to be done.

verses.text: Without Thy counsel and providence, and without cause, nothing cometh to pass on the earth.
verses.modernizedText: Without Your counsel and providence, and without cause, nothing happens on earth.

verses.text: It is good for me, Lord, that I had been in trouble, that I may learn Thy statutes,(4) and may cast away all pride of heart and presumption.
verses.modernizedText: It is good for me, Lord, that I have been in trouble, so that I may learn Your statutes,(4) and cast away all pride of heart and presumption.

verses.text: It is profitable for me that confusion hath covered my face, that I may seek to Thee for consolation rather than unto men.
verses.modernizedText: It is profitable for me that confusion has covered my face, so that I may seek consolation from You rather than from people.

verses.text: By this also I have learned to dread Thine unsearchable judgment, who afflictest the just with the wicked, but not without equity and justice.
verses.modernizedText: Through this I have also learned to fear Your unsearchable judgment, who afflict the just with the wicked, but not without equity and justice.

verses.text: Thanks be unto Thee, because Thou hast not spared my sins, but hast beaten me with stripes of love, inflicting pains, and sending troubles upon me without and within.
verses.modernizedText: Thanks be to You, because You have not spared my sins, but have beaten me with stripes of love, inflicting pains and sending troubles upon me without and within.

verses.text: There is none who can console me, of all things which are under heaven, but Thou only, O Lord my God, Thou heavenly Physician of souls, who dost scourge and hast mercy, who leadest down to hell and bringest up again.(5) Thy discipline over me, and Thy rod itself shall teach me.
verses.modernizedText: Of all things under heaven, there is no one who can console me but You alone, O Lord my God, heavenly Physician of souls, who scourge and have mercy, who lead down to hell and bring up again.(5) Your discipline over me and Your very rod will teach me.

verses.text: Behold, O beloved Father, I am in Thy hands, I bow myself under the rod of Thy correction.
verses.modernizedText: See, O beloved Father, I am in Your hands; I bow myself under the rod of Your correction.

verses.text: Smite my back and my neck that I may bend my crookedness to Thy will.
verses.modernizedText: Strike my back and my neck, so that I may bend my crookedness to Your will.

verses.text: Make me a pious and lowly disciple, as Thou wert wont to be kind, that I may walk according to every nod of Thine.
verses.modernizedText: Make me a devout and humble disciple, as You have always been kind, so that I may walk according to Your every nod.

verses.text: To Thee I commend myself and all that I have for correction; better is it to be punished here than hereafter.
verses.modernizedText: To You I commend myself and all that I have for correction; it is better to be punished here than hereafter.

verses.text: Thou knowest all things and each of them; and nothing remaineth hid from Thee in man’s conscience.
verses.modernizedText: You know all things and each one of them, and nothing in a person’s conscience remains hidden from You.

verses.text: Before they are, thou knowest that they will be, and Thou needest not that any man teach Thee or admonish Thee concerning the things which are done upon the earth.
verses.modernizedText: Before things happen, You know that they will be, and You do not need anyone to teach or remind You about what is done on earth.

verses.text: Thou knowest what is expedient for my profit, and how greatly trouble serveth unto the scrubbing off the rust of sin.
verses.modernizedText: You know what is useful for my profit and how greatly trouble serves to scrub off the rust of sin.

verses.text: Do with me according to Thy desired good pleasure, and despise not my life which is full of sin, known to none so entirely and fully as to Thee alone.
verses.modernizedText: Deal with me according to Your desired good pleasure, and do not despise my life, which is full of sin and known completely and fully to You alone.

verses.text: Grant me, O Lord, to know that which ought to be known; to love that which ought to be loved; to praise that which pleaseth Thee most, to esteem that which is precious in Thy sight, to blame that which is vile in Thine eyes.
verses.modernizedText: Grant me, O Lord, to know what ought to be known, to love what ought to be loved, to praise what pleases You most, to esteem what is precious in Your sight, and to blame what is vile in Your eyes.

verses.text: Suffer me not to judge according to the sight of bodily eyes, nor to give sentence according to the hearing of the ears of ignorant men; but to discern in true judgment between visible and spiritual things, and above all things to be ever seeking after the will of Thy good pleasure.
verses.modernizedText: Do not allow me to judge by what bodily eyes see or give sentence according to what the ears hear from ignorant people, but let me discern with true judgment between visible and spiritual things and above all always seek the will of Your good pleasure.

verses.text: Oftentimes the senses of men are deceived in judging; the lovers of the world also are deceived in that they love only visible things.
verses.modernizedText: Often the senses of people are deceived in judging; lovers of the world are also deceived in loving only visible things.

verses.text: What is a man better because by man he is reckoned very great?
verses.modernizedText: How is a person better because another considers him very great?

verses.text: The deceiver deceiveth the deceiver, the vain man the vain, the blind man the blind, the weak man the weak, when they exalt one another; and in truth they rather put to shame, while they foolishly praise.
verses.modernizedText: The deceiver deceives the deceiver, the vain the vain, the blind the blind, the weak the weak, when they exalt one another; and in truth they rather put one another to shame while they foolishly praise.

verses.text: For as humble St. Francis saith, “What each one is in Thine eyes, so much he is, and no more.”
verses.modernizedText: For as humble St. Francis says, “What each one is in Your eyes, that much he is, and no more.”
